title: Lesson 34: Data Model Design: Inheritance, Polymorphic Relationships, and Denormalization Tradeoffs
description: Three tools for records that stop being uniform: inheritance for kinds of a thing, polymorphic relationships for one field pointing at many things, and denormalization for paying write cost to make reads fast.

questions.question: A custom object must reference an Account, an Opportunity, or a Case, and all three already relate to one Account. What is the sound modeling choice?
options: Add a custom polymorphic field that can point at any of the three objects.
Point the record at the shared Account as a normal lookup.
Create three separate versions of the object, one for each parent type.
Store the parent type and the parent Id in two separate text fields.
questions.explanation: When the candidate parents share a meaningful common ancestor, pointing at the ancestor turns a wild polymorphic field into a normal, reportable, securable lookup that every query and report can handle.

questions.question: Two subtypes of one concept share almost no fields or relationships. Why is one object with record types a poor fit?
options: Record types cannot be reported on across all subtypes in one place.
Record types cannot give each subtype its own layout, picklist values, or required fields.
Record types hide fields from the user, not the database.
Record types prevent an object from having a sharing and security model.
questions.explanation: A record type only hides a field from the user, never from the database, so deeply divergent subtypes pile meaningless fields onto one object; separate objects behind a shared supertype fit better.

questions.question: What does a roll-up summary field require and cost in exchange for showing a parent aggregate without an aggregate query?
options: A master-detail relationship plus write cost on the parent per child change.
A lookup relationship and manual refresh whenever the aggregate should update.
No stored value and a recomputation of the aggregate on every read.
Indexable storage that offsets its cost by making filters faster.
questions.explanation: A roll-up summary is platform-maintained denormalization: it needs a master-detail relationship and adds write work on the parent each time a child changes, in return for a cached aggregate on read.
